Answer-level $\kappa$ may underestimate the independence bottleneck: two traces can follow nearly identical reasoning yet reach different final answers, causing $\kappa$ to treat them as disagreeing. On Mistral-7B FOLIO ($n = 204$), the mean pairwise cosine similarity of chain-of-thought traces (TF-IDF, Eq.~\ref{eq:process-sim}) is $0.69$, far exceeding answer-level $\kappa = 0.41$. These measures are uncorrelated ($r = -0.06$, $p = 0.36$): problems with diverse answers do not exhibit diverse reasoning. We find 9.3\% of trace pairs converge on reasoning ($\cos > 0.8$) while disagreeing on the final answer---apparent answer diversity masking process-level homogeneity.

Figure~\ref{fig:process-kappa} (Appendix~\ref{app:process-kappa-fig}) visualizes this decoupling. This gap implies that interventions targeting answer diversity (temperature scaling, diverse prompting) may spread answers without altering reasoning paths.

- §1 Intro: 25+ same-model interventions all fail → independence bottleneck → two independent cures
- §2 Related Work
- §3 Diagnostic Framework: Independence Bottleneck (process-κ, Eff-K, oracle gap)
- §4 Symbolic Confirmation Bias: bias ratio 4.97×, overlap rate 94%

- Conservative truncation: 65.7% accuracy
- SC baseline: 54.41%, SICA baseline: 59.31%
- Delta: +11.3pp vs SC, +6.4pp vs SICA

**等待**: G 全量结果 (204/204) 和 G+R combo 实验。目前先更新 writing_plan.yaml 和章节规划，G 全量到后立即 Patch。

    Symbolic confirmation bias (4.97× bias ratio) causes self-extracted
    FOL constraints to confirm LLM trace answers regardless of correctness.
    Two independent cures with different mechanisms: (1) Constraint-Answer

    independent solutions with different mechanisms (G=info-flow, R=arch-diversity)
  framing: >

      yields maximal effect, confirming bias concentrates in conclusion
      sentences. Zero-cost intervention requiring no additional model.
    registry_refs: [exp-wave3-dir-g-decoupling]

    registry_refs: [exp-wave3-dir-r-nli-verifier, exp-wave3-dir-r-combo-extended]

    status: VERIFIED
    claim: >

      r=-0.06 (p=0.36). 9.3% trace pairs show convergent reasoning.
    registry_refs: [exp-wild4-process-kappa]

\paragraph{Parameters.} $K{=}12$ traces at $T{=}0.7$; extraction at $T_{\text{ext}}{=}0.3$. Z3 timeout: 10s. $\alpha{=}0.5$. Statistical significance via McNemar exact test ($\alpha{=}0.05$); 95\% bootstrap CIs from 10,000 resamples for $n \geq 200$.

\paragraph{Computational cost.} On Mistral-7B FOLIO ($K{=}12$), SICA takes $4.5{\times}$ the wall-clock time of SC (81.4 vs.\ 17.7\,min for 204 questions). The bottleneck is constraint extraction---$K$ additional LLM calls per question consuming 76\% of total time (17.8\,s/question)---while trace generation (shared with SC, 5.2\,s) accounts for 22\% and Z3 solving is negligible (3\,ms, ${<}0.1\%$). For comparison: ICG requires $3.2{\times}$, Debate $10.5{\times}$, and Contrastive $10.9{\times}$ of SC time. The $4.5{\times}$ overhead yields no significant accuracy gain, underscoring the practical cost of the confirmation bias bottleneck.
